name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years, from the arrival of the first vanguard to pushing the defenders back to their mightiest cities. A dark future hangs over the Iron Kingdoms—will you stand firm against the invasion, or will you join it and revel in the spoils of war?

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons, with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player will choose to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games of the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Over the course of the campaign, players will track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles. Each player will be responsible to keep a tally of their own War Chest points. At the end of the third chapter, a player’s War Chest total will be used to rate that player’s performance as either an Invader of the Iron Kingdoms or as one of its valiant Defenders. War Chest points are awarded as follows: -Playing a Campaign Game: 1 point -Winning a Key Battle: +1 point -Winning by Killing the Opposing Leader: +1 point -Winning by Scenario Victory Conditions: +2 points

name: Name
body: Black Tide campaign scenarios are intended to be played in order. Each scenario grants the winning player, either the Invader or the Defender, an advantage in the subsequent scenario. Advantages are one-use only and can only be used the first time the winning player plays the scenario that follows the scenario in which the advantage was awarded.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Due to the nature of these scenarios, with the Invader sometimes striking the Defender without warning from sea or under the cover of darkness, the Invading player will not be allowed to place Defenses in same cases. It will be noted in the Terrain Placement section of each scenario whether the Invader can place Defenses or not.

name: Name
body: A flag is a scenario marker on a 40 mm base. A flag, however, is not a model. Models cannot end their movement on flags or be placed on them for any reason. A model can move through a flag if it has enough movement to move completely past it. While playing a Black Tide scenario, a player controls a flag when one or more of non-Cohort models are B2B with the flag and none of their opponent’s models contest it. A flag is contested if one or more of your opponent’s models are within 4" of it. Inert warjacks and wild warbeasts cannot contest flags.

name: Name
body: Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle gains an additional War Chest point.

name: Name
body:
In the days to come, we will say we had no warning.
We will lie to ourselves, to salve our shame and cover our fear. We will claim that even the wisest among us could never have foreseen this end, even as those wisest lie dead around us.
Our memories are too short, and we will not speak of the scent of blood on the salt air or the malice of dark clouds on the distant horizon that preceded their coming. The chill in the summer air that whispered of hate and led hardened sailors to shelter on the shore rather than brave the waters. These warnings will be lost in the flood of terror, panic, and blood that followed.
Ioseph’s boat was the first to disappear, him with both his sons. Most said an ill tide or rogue storm took him. Those who would be cruel faulted poor seamanship and drunkenness. Those who thought themselves clever spoke of pirates and bandits.
He was a proud and faithful child of Morrow. I wonder if that gave him peace in the end.
In truth, our warning came long before my oars first tasted the sea. It came as a curse, shouted in spite from the last of the oppressors’ ships as they sailed away from our shores. For four hundred years, we buried that warning in prosperity, in willful ignorance, drowning it in the idle waters of denial. Those memories became grey and faded with time, and we told ourselves that their final promise would never come to pass.

name: Name
body:
In the days to come, we will say to ourselves we had no warning.
Dark sails now fill the horizon, bearing fire and iron, spite and ripened hate. We will find those words to be of little comfort in the end.
—Unknown fisherman, Khador

name: Name
body: Under the cover of a rising storm, the invaders’ vanguard arrives: a lightning strike to silence the warning beacons and secure their fleet’s approach to the beach. While dark sails wait beyond the horizon, a smaller force rows to shore against the unsuspecting defenders. A single lighthouse guards this turn of the coast, and if the light goes out, hope will soon follow.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Invaders attempt to tear down a lighthouse tower while the Defenders fight to defend it until the warning signal can be lit.

name: Name
body: Scenario 1 is suitable for 50 point armies.

name: Name
body: Place a structure at least 5" in diameter in the middle of the table centered 18" forward from the Defender’s Deployment Zone, as shown on the map. This represents the Tower.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each placing up to 4 features. After these terrain features have been placed, the Defender may place up to 3 Defenses on their side of the table outside of their Deployment Zone. The Invader cannot place Defenses when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: -"The Light Goes Out": The Tower is a structure that is friendly to the Defender. It has DEF 5, ARM 20, and 40 Damage Boxes. -"The Rising Storm": Models lose Flight and cannot gain Flight while playing this scenario. -"Spotters": At the beginning of the Defender’s turn, the Defender can choose one enemy model to be illuminated by the Tower. That model loses Stealth and suffers –2 DEF against ranged attacks this turn. -"Invasion": The Invader is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
The Invader immediately wins the match if they control the only Leader model in play. (the Invader gains +1 War Chest point)
If the Tower is destroyed, the Invaders immediately win the match. (the Invader gains +2 War Chest points)
If the Tower has not been destroyed by the end of the Invader’s sixth turn, or if the Invader’s Leader is killed, the Defender wins the match. (the Defender gains +2 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins this match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #2: Sea Assault, that player’s models gain Stealth during the first turn.
If the Defender player wins this match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #2: Sea Assault, that player can choose up to three units to gain Advance Deployment.

name: Name
body: Ships laden with soldiers, beasts, and machines of war churn up the surf as they race to the shore, crashing up onto the sand and beaching themselves with the groan of wooden planks and iron paddles. The warriors within spill out, their feet defiling the ground beneath them in the first steps of their conquest. But they are not alone, and ahead, the defenders and their hasty fortifications prepare to meet them head-on.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Invader lands on the beaches and tries to push up to seize points along the shore while the Defender fights to repel the assault.

name: Name
body: 50–75 point armies

name: Name
body:
Before placing other terrain, place three 40 mm flag markers on the table 12" forward from the rear edge of the Defender’s Deployment Zone as shown on the map below.
Draw a line 10" forward from the rear edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone. This represents the shore. All space between the rear edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone and this line is considered shallow water. The Invader then places four 6"×12" structures on the table to represent landing ships. These structures can be placed anywhere on the table, but part of each landing ship must touch the rear edge of the Invader’s Deployment Zone.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each placing up to 4 features.  After these terrain features have been placed, the Defender may place up to 4 Defenses on their side of the table outside of their Deployment Zone. The Invader cannot place Defenses when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: -Beach Landing: The Invaders do not deploy normally. Instead, before the game begins, the Invader secretly assigns each of their models/units to one of the four landing ships. After the Defender has deployed their non-Advance Deploying models, the Invader deploys their army with each model/unit in base contact with the landing ship they were assigned to. -From the Sea: The Invader is the first player when playing this scenario. When playing this scenario, the Invader’s models lose Advance Deployment and Ambush.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play (the winning player gains +2 War Chest point)
The Invader wins the match if, at any time, they control any two of the three flags. (the Invader gains +3 War Chest points)
The Defender wins the match if the Invader has not won by the end of their sixth turn (the Defender gains +3 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #3: Breakout, once during the game at the start of any of their Control Phases, they can return one friendly destroyed non-character model/unit to play, placing it completely within their Deployment Zone. Models are returned with all of their damage boxes unmarked.
If the Defender player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #3: Breakout, once during the game at start of any of their turns they can choose one friendly model/unit whose melee weapons gain Beat Back this turn. (Immediately after a basic attack with a weapon with Beat Back is resolved during this model’s Combat Action, the enemy model hit can be pushed 1" directly away from the attacking model. After the enemy model is pushed, the attacking model can advance up to 1" directly toward it".)

name: Name
body: As bodies mount up on the beach, the invaders push back against the defensive lines struggling to contain them. Again, they crash against the stalwart guardians of the nation beyond, and again they are turned back, confined to their beachhead. Tension hangs in the air as the next charge readies, the roar of terrible creatures and the fires of warjacks signaling another advance into the battered lines.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, both sides fight to control the no-man’s-land between their forces while both defending their own trench and trying to seize the enemy’s trench. Each side carries a flag as well, which can inspire their troops forward or become an enemy’s trophy of war.

name: Name
body: 50–75 point armies

name: Name
body:
Place two 40 mm flag markers on the table as shown on the map below.
Mark out two 3" wide trenches across the table as shown on the map.
A model completely within a trench has cover from attacks made by models that are not touching the trench that the model is in. Models completely within a trench gain Resistance: Blast.
A player controls a trench if at least one of their models is completely within the trench and none of their opponent’s models are within it.

name: Name
body:
Players alternate placing terrain features, with each placing up to 4 features. Players can then place Defenses normally.
Terrain features (including Defenses) cannot be placed in the area between the two trenches.

name: Name
body: -Flagbearer: After both players have deployed their armies, each player selects one non-Leader, warrior model to be the flagbearer. Add a flag token to this model. If your flagbearer ends its Normal Movement closer to the rear edge of your opponent’s Deployment Zone than where it began, each friendly model with LOS to the flagbearer that begins its Normal Movement closer to the rear edge of your Deployment Zone than the flagbearer does gains +2 SPD that activation. -Take Up the Colors: If the flagbearer is destroyed or removed from play, before removing it from the table, center the flag token on its location. Another non-Leader, warrior model that advances into contact with the flag token or is placed in contact with it can pick it up and become the flagbearer. Place the flag token on this model. -Nightfall: At the beginning of the first player’s fourth turn, all models gain Concealment for the rest of the match.

name: Name
body:
Starting on the second player’s second turn, at the end of each player’s turn, each player scores 1 Control Point (CP) for each flag they control, 1 CP if they control the trench on their side of the table, and 3 CP if they control the trench on their opponent’s side of the table.
If a player’s model advance ends its movement in contact with an enemy’s flag token or is placed in contact with it, that player can choose to immediately destroy the flag token. If a flag token is destroyed, the destroying player gains 2 CP and the flag token is removed from the table.

name: Name
body:
A player immediately wins if they control the only Leader model in play. (the winning player gains +1 War Chest point)
If a player has 5 or more points than their opponent at the end of their opponent’s turn, that player wins. (the winning player gains +2 War Chest points)
If the game does not end before the end of the second player’s seventh turn, the player with the most CP wins the game. (the winning player gains +2 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, the Evacuation scenario in the next chapter, once during the game at the start of any of their turns, that player can choose to give their Leader model Inspiring Charge that turn. (When a model with Inspiring Charge or another friendly model within 6" of that model declares a charge, the charging models gains +3 SPD when resolving the charge.)
If the Defender player wins the match, when playing next scenario, the Evacuation scenario in the next chapter, once during the game at the end of any of their turns, they can choose to give all of their units the Battle-Driven special rule for one round. (Battle-Driven: When one or more models in this unit are damaged by an enemy attack, after the attack is resolved models in this unit gain +2 ARM, +2 to their melee attack damage rolls, and Pathfinder for one round.)
